intros.text: Groucho Marx once quipped, "Politics is the art of looking for trouble, finding it everywhere, diagnosing it incorrectly, and applying the wrong remedy." This cynical view sets the stage for our discussion.

intros.text: "Politics is the art of the possible, but ethics is the art of the right." — Otto von Bismarck (attributed)
Politics denotes the authoritative allocation of values in a society; ethics denotes the reasoned principles that judge those allocations as just or unjust.
When a municipal councillor refuses a bribe to award a contract, the act is both political (resource allocation) and ethical (integrity).
